title: Appearance holds what a shape is, Effects is a list you add to
goal: A rectangle shows an Appearance panel and an Effects panel and it is not clear what belongs in which: both appear to carry an opacity and a corner radius. Split them on a rule anyone can state. Appearance holds the things every shape simply has, in the same order every time, starting with opacity, then its fill and its outline, and a corner radius only on shapes that have corners. Effects is a list you add to on demand: a border, a glow, a shadow, a blur, and later filters. You can add more than one of a kind, so two borders with different offsets give you an inner and an outer one. You can select an effect to change it, remove it, or drag it to change the order things paint in. Appearance sits directly under the layers panel and above Effects.
notes: Rewritten on 2026-09-07 after the user saw the shipped Appearance list beside the older Effects section and could not tell what belonged where. Their split, which supersedes the earlier proposal in this task: Appearance is what a shape intrinsically has, Effects is an addable list. Note that the duplication they report is partly an illusion worth fixing on its own: in their screenshot the Blur, Size, Distance, Direction and Opacity under Appearance are the SHADOW's settings, shown inline beneath the Shadow row by the change that landed the same day, while Effects carries the layer's own opacity, blur and corner radius. Because the inline settings carry no sign of which part owns them, a shadow's blur reads as a second top level blur. So the panel needs a visible owner for a part's settings whatever else is decided, which is why that is its own acceptance item. Two ideas from the earlier draft still hold and should be kept: inner versus outer is a property of an effect rather than a separate effect, which the user has now confirmed by asking for an offset on a border; and once the list is addable, order becomes visible and must be draggable. Read Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerParts.swift and Sources/Photonz/PartsInspector.swift, and coordinate with switching-a-part-on-shows-its-settings-straight, which changes how a row reveals its settings, so the two do not fight.
acceptance: Write the split down in the design docs first: what makes something an appearance property rather than an effect, and the fixed order Appearance uses
Open a decision card showing the two panels drawn under this split, with a shape carrying two borders and a shadow, and wait for the answer
Appearance shows opacity first, then fill and outline, in the same order for every kind of shape, and shows a corner radius only where corners exist
No control appears in both panels, and nothing in either is named the same as something in the other unless they are genuinely the same setting
Blur moves out of Appearance and becomes an effect you add
Effects starts empty on a new shape and gains rows only when you add them, from one obvious gesture that needs no dialog
The same kind of effect can be added more than once, each with its own settings, including an offset on a border so an inner and an outer one are two rows
An effect row can be selected, removed, and dragged to reorder, and reordering visibly changes what paints over what
A part's settings are visibly owned by that part, so a shadow's own blur can never be mistaken for the layer's blur
Appearance sits directly below the layers panel and above Effects, and stays there
Every effect the app already draws keeps drawing exactly as it does, and existing documents are untouched
The model is written so a new effect is a new kind in the list and nothing else has to change to accept it, and the audit names the next two that would be added and how
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a shape carrying two borders, a shadow and a blur, and the panels in order, anything rough filed as a follow-up

Read the model as built: LayerPart has three cases; LayerStyle carries one optional ShadowStyle; DocumentRenderer paints shadow, fill, border in a fixed order.

Adversarial review, before building. 1) A picture/frame/label ring is ALREADY an inside border (DocumentRenderer.bordered insets the box by the full width and cuts the middle out) and a shape stroke is ALREADY centred (AnnotationRasterizer strokes the path). So a Position setting cannot have one default across layer kinds without repainting existing documents: it must default to Inside for a ring and Centre for a shape.

Adversarial review 2) Collapsing inner and outer into a popup makes the add menu useless and hurts discovery: a person hunting for an inner shadow scans for those two words. Resolution kept in the model: the add menu names Shadow and Inner shadow separately, and both add ONE Shadow row with its Kind preset. One row type, two doors in.

Adversarial review 3) Off and remove are two ways to make a thing go away, which is the real hazard. Resolution: only countable kinds carry a remove, so a plain rectangle has exactly one gesture and remove only appears once you have added a second of something.

Adversarial review 4) The biggest collision is with what shipped yesterday: settings always showing. With one shadow that is right; with two it is twelve slider rows. Measured on the mock strips: today 503 pt, option A 889 pt, option B 561 pt. That is a UX judgement with a visible consequence, so it is in the decision rather than decided here.

Adversarial review 5) Reorder by drag is the most expensive piece and the least visible: between two drop shadows the difference only shows where they overlap. It is kept because it becomes real the moment an inner shadow can sit above or below the fill, but it is called out as the first thing to cut if the build runs long.

Adversarial review 6) Multi-selection needs a rule the fixed list never needed. Written into the doc: rows line up by position in the list, not by kind, and a row that reaches fewer layers says so with the sentence Fill already uses.

Model written down: docs/design/shape-parts.md, new section How the list grows. Kinds table (name, count, colour, settings), what order means, off vs remove, the two render facts that bind the defaults, and how a new kind arrives.
Mock strips rendered: Scripts/make-appearance-list-mock.swift draws the same rectangle (fill, inside border, two drop shadows) under today and three models.

The task was rewritten by the user mid-run (Appearance vs Effects split). What had already been built to the OLD brief shipped anyway, because it is needed under every answer to the new one: b90ea5c7.

Shipped: LayerStyle.shadows is a list, nearest the eye first; `shadow` still reads/writes the first so nothing written before this broke. ShadowStyle gains kind (drop/inner) and isOn. A file with one shadow saves the same bytes; two writes the first where it always was, so an older build still draws it.

Shipped: renderer walks the list. Inner shadows cast into the layer clipped to its silhouette, drops go behind, nearest the eye first. Perf unchanged for 0 or 1 drop shadow. Tests: AppearanceListTests (18), ShadowListRenderTests (6).

Shipped: panel is a list you add to. Plus on the Appearance HEADER (not the foot, which the card had shown: the dock caps a section's height and scrolls the rest inside it, and one shadow already pushes a foot button out of sight). Kind popup, cross to remove, grip to drag, and a right-click row menu that does the same three in words.

Bug found and fixed on the way: with TWO shadows the whole right hand dock closed itself. The Kind popup asked for its ideal width (.fixedSize), the pane grew wider than the window, and the shell auto-collapsed the dock. It has a width now. Reproduced and confirmed fixed on the probe.

Outline Position (inside/centre/outside) NOT built, and the earlier note in this log about a shape's stroke being centred was wrong: AnnotationRasterizer insets the box by strokeWidth/2 and strokes, so the stroke lands wholly INSIDE the frame, exactly like a picture's ring. Inside is the only position anything in the app has ever drawn. Outside needs the rasterizer padded and Layer.renderBounds / previewPadding grown, which is a piece of work of its own: filed as a-border-can-sit-outside-the-edge-not-only-insid.

Verified on the probe with Scripts/playtest/appearance-list-walk.json (status ok, real screen captures, Screen Recording granted). The walk cannot drive the grip: a synthesized press cannot start a SwiftUI drag. Reorder is covered by core tests plus a render test that proves two shadows of different colours swap which is on top.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the real app: two shadows do NOT fit. A shadow costs seven rows, so the second shadow's own row is already below the fold of the Appearance section and a playtest press on it fails the reach check. That is the density option B of the first card was about, now real rather than predicted. It is in the audit's rough and it is why the new split matters.
